subject.title: fix(cli-runner): use sender metadata in CLI session history user labels

question: Should CLI reseed history expose persisted group sender identity to the model, and what sanitization contract must apply to that untrusted metadata?
rationale: The merged persistence work intentionally did not change model-visible prompt content; choosing to expose durable participant identity is a cross-session trust and product-policy decision, not a mechanical renderer choice.

options.title: Approve scoped attribution after hardening
options.body: Allow envelope-only sender labels for group-history reseed prompts after removing all unsafe control characters and adding persisted-session proof.

options.title: Keep identity persistence non-model-visible
options.body: Retain the current metadata persistence for transcript tooling while leaving reseed history at the stable `User:` label.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped attribution after hardening
recommendation.body: Allow envelope-only sender labels for group-history reseed prompts after removing all unsafe control characters and adding persisted-session proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the persisted sender-metadata contract whose intended consumers and trust boundary this PR expands.
